1.title: The Best of Dubai in 24 Hours

periods.title: Old Dubai: Creek, Souks & Heritage
periods.text: Start early at Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, narrow lanes with traditional wind-tower buildings dating to the 1800s. Take an abra (AED 1) across Dubai Creek to the Spice Souk and Gold Souk in Deira. The sensory overload of saffron, incense, and glittering gold is unforgettable. Grab a chai at a waterfront cafe and watch the dhow boats.
periods.tip: The abra ride is the best AED 1 you'll spend in Dubai: pure old-world charm with the skyline behind you.

periods.title: Downtown Dubai & Burj Khalifa
periods.text: Metro to Downtown Dubai. Walk through Dubai Mall. The aquarium tunnel is visible free from the mall walkway. Head up the Burj Khalifa "At the Top" observation deck, levels 124–125 (AED 179 non-peak online). Lunch at one of the food courts, surprisingly affordable at AED 30–50 for a full meal with Burj Khalifa views.
periods.tip: Book the late afternoon slot (4–5pm). You'll get daylight views, sunset, and the city lighting up.

periods.title: Dubai Fountain, Street Food & Nightlife
periods.text: The Dubai Fountain show starts at 6pm (every 30 minutes, free). Watch two shows. Each is different. Walk to Satwa for dinner at Ravi Restaurant (Pakistani curries, AED 25–40, cash only) and karak chai on Al Dhiyafah Road. If you have energy, head to Dubai Marina for waterfront drinks. Happy hours run until 7pm with drinks from AED 25.
periods.tip: Time the fountain shows with sunset. Arrive at 5:30pm for a front-row seat along the Burj Khalifa Lake promenade.

periods.title: Al Fahidi & Dubai Creek
periods.text: Start at the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, narrow lanes lined with traditional wind-tower buildings dating to the 1800s. Visit the Coffee Museum (AED 10, includes a free cup), browse XVA Gallery, then take an abra (traditional wooden boat, AED 1) across Dubai Creek to explore the Spice Souk and Gold Souk in Deira.
periods.tip: The abra ride is the best AED 1 you'll spend in Dubai: pure old-world charm with the skyline behind you.

periods.title: Al Seef & Culture
periods.text: Lunch at a Bur Dubai Indian cafeteria, a full thali platter for AED 15–20. Then stroll the Al Seef waterfront promenade, a heritage district blending restored buildings with contemporary design. Visit the Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding for a guided session with local Emirati hosts.
periods.tip: Al Seef is one of Dubai's most photogenic spots and barely appears in tourist guides.

periods.title: Dubai Frame & Satwa Street Food
periods.text: Metro to Zabeel Park for the Dubai Frame (AED 50), a 150m-tall frame offering contrasting views of old and new Dubai from its glass-bottomed sky bridge at sunset. Dinner at the legendary Ravi Restaurant in Satwa: Pakistani curries and kebabs for AED 25–40. Cash only. Then wander Al Dhiyafah Road for karak chai.
periods.tip: Time your Dubai Frame visit for 30 minutes before sunset. You'll get both the golden hour and nighttime cityscapes.

periods.title: JBR Beach & Marina
periods.text: Morning at JBR Beach (free public access) while it's quiet. Walk The Walk at JBR promenade: cafes, shops, and views of the world's largest observation wheel, Ain Dubai. Feeling brave? Book the XLine zipline at Dubai Marina: 1km at 80km/h, 170m above the marina (from AED 499).
periods.tip: JBR is quieter before 10am on weekdays. Grab a coffee at a beachfront cafe and enjoy the calm.

periods.title: Downtown & Burj Khalifa
periods.text: Metro to Downtown Dubai. Walk through Dubai Mall. The aquarium tunnel is visible for free from the mall walkway. Head up the Burj Khalifa "At the Top" observation deck, levels 124–125. Book a non-peak slot online (AED 179 vs AED 250 peak, saves AED 40–50 vs counter).
periods.tip: Book the after-8pm slot, cheaper than peak hours and you get the city lit up at night.

periods.title: Dubai Fountain & Marina Nightlife
periods.text: The Dubai Fountain show runs every 30 minutes from 6pm, free and mesmerizing against the Burj Khalifa. Watch at least two shows. Then head to Dubai Marina for the evening. Walk Marina Walk for the illuminated skyline, and hit Bla Bla or Zero Gravity for drinks. Happy hours run 1–7pm at most venues (drinks from AED 25).
periods.tip: The Guzzler app shows real-time happy hour deals across the city. Ladies' nights (Tue–Thu) often mean free drinks for women.

periods.title: Alserkal Avenue Art District
periods.text: Explore Alserkal Avenue in Al Quoz, a converted industrial warehouse complex now housing contemporary art galleries (free entry), indie cafes, and Cinema Akil (art-house cinema). Grab speciality coffee here. Then taxi to the Museum of the Future on Sheikh Zayed Road. Even the calligraphy-covered exterior is worth the trip.
periods.tip: Alserkal is Dubai's creative soul, the antithesis of the glitz. Don't skip it.

periods.title: Satwa Lunch & Desert Prep
periods.text: Lunch at Al Mallah on Al Dhiyafah Road: legendary shawarma for AED 8–10 and fresh juices under AED 15. A full lunch comes to AED 20–30. Head back to rest and get ready for the desert safari. Most operators pick up from hotels around 3–3:30pm.
periods.tip: Al Mallah's AED 8 chicken shawarma rivals versions costing three times more elsewhere in the city.

periods.title: Desert Safari
periods.text: The quintessential Dubai experience. Hotel pickup, 45-minute drive to the dunes, then 30–40 minutes of adrenaline-pumping dune bashing in a 4x4. Stop for sunset photos over the dunes, then arrive at a Bedouin-style camp for sandboarding, camel rides, henna painting, and a barbecue dinner under the stars. Budget group tours from AED 130–200.
periods.tip: Book online through discount platforms, not your hotel concierge. It saves 30–50% on the same experience.

periods.tip: JBR is quieter before 10am on weekdays. Grab a coffee at a beachfront cafe and enjoy the calm.

periods.title: Downtown & Burj Khalifa
periods.text: Metro to Downtown Dubai. Walk through Dubai Mall. The aquarium tunnel is visible for free from the mall walkway. Head up the Burj Khalifa "At the Top" observation deck (AED 179 non-peak online). Explore City Walk for lunch, a more local, design-focused district with great cafes.
periods.tip: Book the after-8pm slot, cheaper than peak hours and you get the city lit up at night.

periods.title: Dubai Fountain & Downtown Dining
periods.text: Dubai Fountain show every 30 minutes from 6pm, free and mesmerizing against the Burj Khalifa. Dinner at one of the Souk Al Bahar restaurants overlooking the fountain, or head to DIFC for cocktails at the atmospheric speakeasy bars.
periods.tip: The boardwalk right on the fountain lake costs AED 5 and puts you closer to the water jets than anywhere else.

periods.title: Alserkal Avenue Art District
periods.text: Explore Alserkal Avenue in Al Quoz, a converted industrial warehouse complex now housing contemporary art galleries (free entry), indie cafes, and Cinema Akil (art-house cinema). This is Dubai's creative heart, far from the glitz.
periods.tip: Alserkal is Dubai's creative soul, the antithesis of the glitz. Don't skip it.

periods.title: Museum of the Future & DIFC
periods.text: Taxi to the Museum of the Future on Sheikh Zayed Road (AED 149). The calligraphy-covered torus building is an architectural icon. Then walk to DIFC (Dubai International Financial Centre), surprisingly good for street art, galleries like Leila Heller, and the Gate Village restaurants.
periods.tip: The Museum of the Future is best mid-afternoon when morning crowds thin out. Book online to skip the queue.

periods.title: La Mer & Jumeirah
periods.text: Head to La Mer beachfront in Jumeirah, a quirky open-air district with street art, boutique shops, and restaurants right on the sand. Dinner at a beachfront restaurant watching the sunset, then walk the Jumeirah Beach promenade.
periods.tip: La Mer is one of the newer districts. It's very Instagram-friendly but also genuinely pleasant for a sunset walk.

periods.title: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
periods.text: Bus from Al Ghubaiba station (AED 25, 2 hours) or split a taxi with fellow travellers (AED 250 total, 1.5 hours). Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is one of the most beautiful buildings on earth: white marble, 82 domes, the world's largest hand-knotted carpet. Free entry but strict dress code (free abayas and kanduras available).
periods.tip: Arrive at opening (9am) to beat the tour buses. The mosque is most photogenic in the morning light.

periods.title: Louvre Abu Dhabi
periods.text: Taxi to the Louvre Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat Island (AED 63 entry). The Jean Nouvel-designed building with its "rain of light" dome is breathtaking. The collection spans 6,000 years of art across civilisations. Allow 2–3 hours minimum. Lunch at the museum cafe with views of the Gulf.
periods.tip: Tuesday–Thursday are quietest. The dome's light pattern is best experienced at noon when the sun is directly overhead.

periods.title: Corniche & Return
periods.text: Walk the Abu Dhabi Corniche, 8km of waterfront promenade with free public beaches. Grab a shawarma from one of the Lebanese restaurants along Hamdan Street (AED 8–12) before catching the bus back to Dubai. The evening bus ride offers a stunning view of the Abu Dhabi skyline receding into the desert.
periods.tip: The last direct bus back to Dubai leaves around 11pm. Check timings to avoid getting stranded.

periods.title: Kite Beach & Watersports
periods.text: Morning at Kite Beach, a more local, active beach than JBR. Rent a paddleboard (AED 80/hour) or try kitesurfing (beginner lessons from AED 350). The beach has a great skatepark, outdoor gym, and food truck area. Views of the Burj Al Arab from the shore.
periods.tip: The food trucks at Kite Beach are excellent value. Try Salt for sliders (AED 25). There's always a queue for a reason.

periods.title: Rest & Prep
periods.text: Head back to rest and recharge. Most desert safari operators pick up from hotels around 3–3:30pm. Use the downtime to explore your neighbourhood. Karama and Bur Dubai have great little cafeterias tucked away in residential blocks.
periods.tip: Top up your water bottle and charge your phone. You'll want both for the desert.

periods.title: Desert Safari
periods.text: The quintessential Dubai experience. Hotel pickup, 45-minute drive to the dunes, then 30–40 minutes of adrenaline-pumping dune bashing in a 4x4. Stop for sunset photos over the dunes, then arrive at a Bedouin-style camp for sandboarding, camel rides, henna painting, and a barbecue dinner under the stars. Budget group tours from AED 130–200.
periods.tip: Book online through discount platforms, not your hotel concierge. It saves 30–50% on the same experience.

periods.title: Global Village or Miracle Garden
periods.text: If visiting Nov–Apr, spend the morning at Global Village (AED 25), a massive open-air cultural market with pavilions from 90+ countries, live entertainment, and incredible street food from around the world. Alternatively, Dubai Miracle Garden (AED 75) has 150 million flowers arranged in stunning displays.
periods.tip: Global Village is most fun in the evening, but mornings are cooler and less crowded for exploring.

periods.title: Deira Fish & Perfume Souks
periods.text: Head to Deira for the areas tourists miss: the Fish Market (fascinating, chaotic, and cheap seafood), the Perfume Souk on Sikkat Al Khail Street (haggle for Arabian oud and attars), and the textile shops of Naif Souk. Lunch at one of the hidden Yemeni restaurants in the back streets: mandi rice and lamb for AED 25–35.
periods.tip: The Perfume Souk vendors will mix custom fragrances for AED 30–50, a unique souvenir that's lighter than a rug.

periods.title: Marina Nightlife
periods.text: Dubai Marina at night is electric. Walk the 7km Marina Walk promenade past superyachts and illuminated towers. For drinks, Bla Bla has a rooftop with panoramic views, or head to Barasti for beach bar vibes. Happy hours run 1–7pm at most venues (drinks from AED 25). Ladies' nights on Tue–Thu mean free drinks for women at many spots.
periods.tip: The Guzzler app shows real-time happy hour deals across the city, essential for budget nightlife.

periods.title: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary
periods.text: A hidden gem: a flamingo reserve in the middle of the city, completely free. Hundreds of Greater Flamingos in a mangrove wetland with the Dubai skyline as a backdrop. Three viewing hides with binoculars provided. Best in the cooler morning hours. Then head to nearby Creek Harbour for breakfast at the waterfront.
periods.tip: The main hide closest to the flamingos opens at 9am. Arrive early for the best light for photography.

periods.title: Last-Minute Shopping & Souvenirs
periods.text: Hit the Karama Market for bargain souvenirs, or the Dubai Mall if you want to pick up duty-free items. For authentic gifts, buy saffron and spice mixes from the Spice Souk, Arabic coffee sets from Al Fahidi, or local dates from Bateel (a premium but worth-it brand). Pack your bags.
periods.tip: Bateel dates make excellent gifts: beautifully packaged, lightweight, and uniquely Dubai. Airport prices are 30% higher.

periods.title: Farewell Dinner
periods.text: For a final splurge, dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Downtown. CÉ LA VI at Address Sky View has Burj Khalifa views and cocktails from AED 60. Or keep it budget at the Al Dhow restaurant on the Creek, a floating dinner cruise with buffet from AED 99. One last look at the skyline before you go.
periods.tip: If your flight is late, most hotels offer day-use rooms or luggage storage. Dubai Airport Terminal 3 has free sleeping pods.

budgetTips.title: Free experiences
budgetTips.text: Dubai Fountain shows, JBR/Kite/Black Palace beaches, Marina Walk, Gold & Spice Souks, Al Fahidi galleries, Alserkal Avenue art district, and the AED 1 Creek abra ride.

budgetTips.title: Eat like a local
budgetTips.text: Bur Dubai, Deira, Satwa, and Karama have cafeterias serving full meals for AED 15–35. Shawarma from street stalls: AED 5–10. Karak chai: AED 1–3.

budgetTips.title: Metro smart
budgetTips.text: Get a Nol Silver Card (AED 25 incl. AED 19 credit). Fares: AED 3–7.50 per ride. All-day pass: AED 22. No eating or gum on the metro (AED 100–200 fine).

budgetTips.title: Book online
budgetTips.text: Burj Khalifa non-peak tickets save AED 70+ vs peak/counter. Desert safaris are 30–50% cheaper through online platforms than hotel concierge.

budgetTips.title: Happy hours
budgetTips.text: Drinks at bars cost AED 40–80 normally. Happy hours (1–7pm) drop to AED 25. Use the Guzzler app. Ladies' nights offer free drinks on Tue/Wed/Thu.

budgetTips.title: Transport
budgetTips.text: Hala Taxi is cheapest, then Careem, then Uber. Avoid taxis during rush hours (7:30–9:30am, 5–7pm). Airport taxi surcharge is AED 25.

budgetBreakdown.notes: Street food & cafeterias → casual dining → fine dining
Free sites & museums → Burj Khalifa + safari → skydive + yacht
Karak chai → happy hours → rooftop bars

practicalInfo.title: Visa & Entry
items: Most nationalities get 30–90 days visa-free on arrival, with no advance application needed
Passport must be valid for 6+ months from entry date
Keep your boarding pass: you may need it for hotel check-in and duty-free purchases

practicalInfo.title: Health & Safety
items: No vaccinations required for entry. Tap water is safe but most people drink bottled
Dubai is extremely safe, with one of the lowest crime rates in the world
Summer heat (Jun–Sep) is dangerous: 40–50°C. Stay hydrated, wear sunscreen, limit outdoor time

practicalInfo.title: Getting Around
items: Dubai Metro: clean, cheap (AED 3–7.50), covers major tourist areas. Get a Nol Silver Card (AED 25)
Careem/Uber are reliable. Hala Taxi is cheapest. Avoid taxis during rush hours (7:30–9:30am, 5–7pm)
Dubai Tram connects Marina to JBR. Water taxis and abras are fun alternatives along the Creek

practicalInfo.title: Connectivity
items: Tourist SIM cards at the airport: du or Etisalat, AED 55–100 for 1–2GB + local calls
Free WiFi in malls, most cafes, and the metro. Hotel WiFi is generally fast
VoIP calls (WhatsApp, FaceTime) are restricted: use a VPN or the Botim app (AED 50/month)

practicalInfo.title: Money
items: AED is pegged to USD (1 USD = 3.67 AED). Currency exchange offices in malls offer better rates than airports
Cards accepted almost everywhere. Carry some cash for souks, street food, and abra rides
Tipping is not mandatory but 10% at restaurants is appreciated. Round up taxi fares

practicalInfo.title: Packing Tips
items: Light, breathable clothing that covers shoulders and knees for public areas and malls
Swimwear for beaches/pools only. A light scarf or shawl for mosque visits and over-air-conditioned malls
Comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen (SPF 50+), sunglasses, and a refillable water bottle

culturalTips.title: Dress Code
culturalTips.text: Cover shoulders and knees in malls and public areas. Swimwear is fine at beaches/pools but cover up when leaving. Mosques require women to cover hair, arms, and legs.

culturalTips.title: Alcohol Rules
culturalTips.text: Only at licensed venues (hotels, bars). Legal age is 21, so carry ID. Being visibly drunk in public is illegal and can lead to arrest.

culturalTips.title: Ramadan
culturalTips.text: No eating, drinking, or smoking in public during daylight hours. Nightlife is toned down. Iftar (sunset meal) is a beautiful cultural experience. Join one.

culturalTips.title: Photography
culturalTips.text: Always ask before photographing people. No photos of government buildings, military, or police. Posting unflattering photos online violates UAE cybercrime laws.

culturalTips.title: Zero Tolerance
culturalTips.text: No drugs (even trace amounts = 4-year minimum sentence). No rude gestures or swearing. No public displays of affection beyond hand-holding for couples.

culturalTips.title: LGBTQ+ Travellers
culturalTips.text: Same-sex relationships are illegal in the UAE. Exercise extreme caution and avoid any public displays of affection.
